title: dedicated-autoscaler: add token-bucket burst controls and per-fleet utilization reporting
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: Customers running Dedicated fleets observed occasional short-duration input spikes that exceeded steady-state throughput and caused request queueing and latency SLO violations. Current autoscaler policies are optimized for sustained load and react too slowly for short bursts. This PR introduces a token-bucket burst control to allow fleets to absorb short bursts without overprovisioning, plus a per-fleet utilization reporting pipeline to make burst behavior observable. Summary of changes: 1) Add TokenBucketController that integrates with the existing DedicatedAutoscaler to track per-fleet burst credits, replenish rate, and maximum burst tokens. 2) Expose new fleet-level config: burst_capacity_tokens, burst_replenish_per_sec, burst_window_seconds. Defaults are conservative (burst_capacity_tokens=1000, replenish=50/s). 3) Modify scaling decisions to consult token bucket before triggering scale-up: if tokens are available, allow short-lived acceptance with higher request prioritization instead of immediate VM/GPU scale-up. 4) Add utilization metrics: dedicated_fleet_burst_credit, dedicated_fleet_burst_consumption_rate, dedicated_fleet_effective_utilization, plus new prometheus labels for fleet_id and pricing_tier. 5) Add a daily aggregation job that samples per-fleet utilization and produces a utilization report endpoint for Console and billing insights. 6) Update autoscaler simulator and unit/integration tests to cover burst windows, corner cases, and failure modes. Design notes: TokenBucketController keeps a durable state in the fleet control plane with optimistic updates; in the event of control plane failure we fall back to existing reactive autoscaling. To avoid cross-fleet interference tokens are strictly scoped to a fleet and cannot be borrowed. The change is feature-flagged (feature.flags.dedicated_burst_control) and off by default. Backwards compatibility: Existing fleet configs remain valid. New config options are optional with safe defaults. Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag. 2) Enable for internal test fleets for 48h smoke. 3) Canary to 5% of Dedicated customers with automatic rollback if error rates or SLO breaches increase beyond threshold. Testing: CI includes new unit tests and an autoscaler lifecycle integration test that simulates burst traffic and validates no unbounded scale-ups. Load tests run in perf-canary to validate cost and latency tradeoffs. Related: references ENG-3214 (autoscaler improvements) and ENG-3301 (observability for Dedicated).
commits: Add TokenBucketController and basic token accounting
Integrate token bucket checks into DedicatedAutoscaler decision path
Add new prometheus metrics and expose them on fleet endpoint
Add config and migration for fleet burst params
Autoscaler simulator tests for burst scenarios
Add daily aggregator job and report endpoint
Update docs and console wiring for utilization report
Fix race condition in token accounting (retry/backoff)
Add feature flag gating and rollout script
review_comments: Rajat Singh: Can you explain the failure mode when control plane writes are delayed? How does token accounting stay consistent across autoscaler replicas?

Ava Martinez: We use optimistic updates with a compare-and-swap on the fleet state record in the control plane; if the CAS fails we retry with backoff. If the control plane is partitioned the autoscaler falls back to reactive scaling (existing behavior). Added a comment in token_bucket_controller.go explaining the invariants.
Maya Patel: Need to make sure metrics cardinality doesn't explode. The new metrics add fleet_id and pricing_tier labels — please confirm fleet_id is coarse (UUID) and pricing_tier is low-cardinality.
Ava Martinez: Confirmed — fleet_id is an existing coarse-level identifier (not per-node). pricing_tier has 3 possible values. Added tests that assert cardinality limits in metrics_registry.
Noah Kim: Will this interact badly with burst-based overprovisioning we do for scheduled maintenance?

Ava Martinez: We treat maintenance overprovisioning as a separate signal. The token bucket only affects acceptance/queueing decisions; scale-up triggered by maintenance override will continue to operate as before. Added an e2e case in autoscaler_burst_test.go.
Maya Patel: CI flaked on integration test once — looks like a race in the simulator harness; can you add deterministic seeding?
Ava Martinez: Added deterministic seed and tightened timing tolerances; re-ran CI locally.
Rajat Singh: Approving after addressing metric cardinality and adding migration script for existing fleet configs.
release_notes: Added token-bucket burst control for Dedicated fleets to allow short-lived spikes to be absorbed without immediate scale-up. New per-fleet utilization metrics and a utilization report endpoint were added. Feature-gated rollout; disabled by default.
